description: Annotated 'Q proof' collage arguing that a wristwatch photo posted by Q was taken inside the Oval Office. The centerpiece is a wide-angle photograph of the Oval Office with several men seated in armchairs and on sofas (decor the caption calls 'Regan Style', i.e. Reagan-era), overlaid with arrows and zoomed crops matching blurred reflections in the watch photo to the room's walls and door. A screenshot of Q drop No.5930643 (03/27/19) showing the watch image and the text 'Marker [2] Set. Q' is inset at bottom, with the large caption 'Q PROOF / Watch is in the Castle / Regan Style'. The people in the Oval Office photo are not identified in the image.
flags: Unverified claim: the collage's assertion that the watch photo was taken in the Oval Office is the creator's interpretation, not established fact
Seated figures in the Oval Office photograph are not identified
'Regan' is the image's own misspelling of Reagan

A screenshot of Q drop No.5930643 (03/27/19) with the watch image and the text 'Marker [2] Set. Q' sits at bottom left, beside the large caption 'Q PROOF / Watch is in the Castle'.
flags: Unverified claim: the collage's assertion that the watch photo was taken in the Oval Office is the creator's interpretation, not established fact

description: Full-page FireShot browser capture of uscode.house.gov displaying the complete text of 18 U.S.C. Chapter 115, 'Treason, Sedition, and Subversive Activities' (Title 18, Part I — Crimes), covering sections 2381 through 2390 with their full statutory text, historical and revision notes, and amendment histories. The capture is extremely long (a whole scrolling webpage) and much of the body text renders very small. In Q-follower context this chapter was shared in connection with drops alleging treason and sedition.
text: 18 USC Ch. 115: TREASON, SEDITION, AND SUBVERSIVE ACTIVITIES. From Title 18—CRIMES AND CRIMINAL PROCEDURE. PART I—CRIMES. CHAPTER 115—TREASON, SEDITION, AND SUBVERSIVE ACTIVITIES. Sec. 2381. Treason. 2382. Misprision of treason. 2383. Rebellion or insurrection. 2384. Seditious conspiracy. 2385. Advocating overthrow of Government. 2386. Registration of certain organizations. 2387. Activities affecting armed forces generally. 2388. Activities affecting armed forces during war. 2389. Recruiting for service against United States. 2390. Enlistment to serve against United States. [2391. Repealed.]. §2381. Treason: Whoever, owing allegiance to the United States, levies war against them or adheres to their enemies, giving them aid and comfort within the United States or elsewhere, is guilty of treason and shall suffer death, or shall be imprisoned not less than five years and fined under this title but not less than $10,000; and shall be incapable of holding any office under the United States. Historical and Revision Notes. Amendments. Effective Date of 1956 Amendment. Repeals. Transfer of Functions.
orgs: U.S. House of Representatives Office of the Law Revision Counsel
flags: FLAGGED FOR MANUAL REVIEW: full-page capture of an entire U.S. Code chapter with thousands of words of statutory text and revision notes, much rendered at very small size — only the chapter heading, section list, and section 2381 text are transcribed verbatim; the remaining sections' full text and notes are not transcribed
